passage: In the polytechnic in a small town the group had a robot project due in ten days. Shalini had not turned up for the last three sessions or sent her drawings. Jatin caught Shalini at the bicycle stand after class, away from the others. "You seem off lately. Is something wrong, or is the work confusing?" Shalini looked down for a moment. "My father is in hospital in the city, and I go back on weekends. I did not want to say." Jatin nodded. "Then tell me which part is hard right now, and we will split the rest." Shalini breathed out. At the next meeting Ravi asked loudly why Shalini was missing, and Jatin said, "It is sorted."

qa.q: Where did Jatin speak to Shalini?
qa.a: Jatin caught Shalini at the bicycle stand after class, away from the others.

qa.q: What might Shalini have been feeling before telling Jatin about the hospital?
qa.a: Shalini was probably worried and tense, carrying a private worry about a family member and not wanting to say; the breath out shows relief when Jatin listened.

qa.q: What made Jatin's private question more helpful than raising it in the meeting?
qa.a: Jatin asked away from the others, without accusing, and offered to split the work, which let Shalini explain and kept the team from judging without knowing.

qa.q: Why might Ravi have asked loudly why Shalini was missing?
qa.a: Ravi may be annoyed at the extra work and unaware of the reason; without the private talk, absence looks like plain avoidance.

grounding: A team member asks a coasting member what is going on in private before escalating, and there is a hidden reason such as family illness.

passage: In a Manchester study group Mei had not touched the shared slides for two weeks. Kai and Priya were quietly furious. Dalia caught Mei at the vending machine. "Hey, no pressure, but what is going on? I noticed your part is empty." Mei shrugged and looked at the machine. "Honestly? I just have not felt like doing it. It seemed boring, and you all were doing fine." Dalia waited a moment. "Okay. It matters to me that the work is shared, so can you take the last slide by Thursday?" Mei sighed. "Fine." Dalia did not add a lecture. By Friday the slide was there, with a note: "Sorry, it was avoidance."

qa.q: How long had Mei not touched the shared slides?
qa.a: Mei had not touched the shared slides for two weeks.

qa.q: Why did Mei say "It seemed boring, and you all were doing fine"?
qa.a: Mei was avoiding the work and assuming others would cover it; the shrug shows little guilt at first, though the note later shows some.

qa.q: What did Dalia do that got the slide done without a fight?
qa.a: Dalia asked privately and calmly, said sharing mattered, and asked for one clear slide by Thursday without a lecture.

qa.q: What might Kai and Priya be feeling while Mei's part stays empty?
qa.a: Kai and Priya are probably angry and worried about the deadline, but quiet about it, letting resentment build without anyone speaking.

grounding: A team member asks a coasting member what is going on in private before escalating, and the reason turns out to be plain avoidance.
